blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as agents, yet it remains unclear how their foundational capabilities translate into agentic capabilities. End-to-end scores leave unresolved whether low benchmark capability or weak deployment drives a failure, limiting actionable diagnosis. We bridge foundational and agentic capabilities through an operation-level measurement framework. We represent each model with a foundational profile derived from capability benchmarks and an operation profile derived from interaction trajectories, and define capability realization gaps as deviations of observed operation performance from predictions based on foundational capabilities. Experiments on fifteen model services in $τ^2$-Bench show that foundational profiles only partially predict agentic operations. Models with comparable profiles can differ substantially in execution, and these gaps remain consistent across task subsets. Operation profiles add information and substantially improve task-score prediction. The framework locates execution departures at the operation level to inform model development and agent evaluation. We will release our code and analysis artifacts.
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型越来越多地被部署为代理,但目前仍不清楚其基础能力如何转化为代理能力。 端到端的分数使基准能力低或部署能力弱都无法解决,这限制了可采取行动的诊断。 我们通过行动一级计量框架,将基础能力和动力能力相接。 我们代表每个模型,其基础剖面取自能力基准,而操作剖面取自相互作用轨迹,并将能力实现差距定义为观测到的操作性能从基于基础能力的预测中偏差. 对15个模型服务的实验(以美元为单位)表明,基础剖面只部分预测了代理操作。 具有可比较特征的模型在执行上可能有很大不同,这些差距在任务子集之间仍然一致。 行动概况增加了信息并大大改进了任务分数预测。 该框架将执行离境定位在业务一级,为模型开发和代理评价提供信息。 我们将公布我们的密码和分析文物。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) have shown considerable promise as agents that interact with users, invoke tools, and respond to environmental feedback over multi-step tasks. This progress has motivated benchmarks for function calling, interactive tool use, and end-to-end task completion ( Patil et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2025 ; Barres et al., 2025 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) . Yet end-to-end scores say little about how foundational benchmark dimensions translate into planning, action selection, and recovery. Connecting these levels separates low benchmark profiles from execution that falls below profile-based expectations.
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型(LLMs)作为与用户互动、援引工具、对多步骤任务的环境反馈作出反应的代理商,显示出相当大的希望。 这一进展推动了功能调用、互动工具使用和端到端任务完成的基准(Patil等人,2025年;Lu等人,2025年;Barres等人,2025年;Luo等人,2025年)。 然而,从端到端的评分对基本基准层面如何转化为规划、行动选择和复苏却无足轻重。 连接这些级别将低基准剖面与低于基于剖面的预期的执行区分开来.

blocks.en: Prior work maps evaluations outside agent environments to aggregate performance ( Song et al., 2026 ) and separately diagnoses intermediate behavior from execution trajectories ( Ou et al., 2025 ) . Linking these views at the operation level lets us test how foundational profiles predict specific execution behaviors and how much task-outcome information process measurements add. Aggregate prediction leaves the execution stage of a capability gap unidentified. A useful account must connect offline capability structure to specific interactive behaviors, generalize across model families, and determine whether those behaviors explain outcome variation left unresolved by benchmark scores. These requirements motivate the questions below.
blocks.zh: 先前的工作绘制了外部代理环境的评价图,以汇总性能(Song等人,2026年),并将中间行为与执行轨迹分开诊断(Ou等人,2025年)。 在操作层面将这些观点联系起来,可以让我们测试基础剖面如何预测具体的执行行为,以及任务结果信息过程的测量能增加多少. 综合预测使能力差距的执行阶段不明。 一个有用的账户必须将离线能力结构与具体的交互行为联系起来,将模型家族中的各种行为概括起来,并确定这些行为是否解释了因基准得分而未解决的结果变化。 这些要求引起了以下问题。

blocks.en: To address this gap, we organize our study around two research questions: RQ1. How well do foundational benchmark scores predict operation scores? and RQ2. Do operation scores provide additional information about overall task performance? Each model receives a foundational profile from capability benchmarks and an operation profile from trajectory annotations; Section 3 defines both. For each provider in turn, we train statistical predictors on the remaining providers and evaluate the excluded provider. Residuals answer RQ1 by locating departures from expected operation scores. The same held-out splits answer RQ2 by comparing foundational, operation, and joint predictors of task performance.

blocks.en: We evaluate model configurations on interaction trajectories from the Banking tasks in τ 2 \tau^{2} -Bench ( Barres et al., 2025 ) . Foundational profiles explain part of the variation in operation scores, with systematic residuals across models and operations. Operation profiles further improve held-out prediction of overall task performance. Our contributions are a framework linking foundational indicators, execution operations, and task outcomes under controlled conditions; a provider-held-out mapping and residual analysis of execution departures; and evidence that combining foundational and operation profiles improves held-out Banking reward prediction.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: End-to-end agent benchmarks evaluate function calling, stateful tool use, dual-control conversations, and interaction with real-world MCP servers, and they primarily report task-level success ( Patil et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2025 ; Barres et al., 2025 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) . Capability- and process-oriented evaluations provide complementary explanations for these outcomes. MMAU separates understanding, reasoning, planning, problem-solving, and self-correction in offline tasks ( Yin et al., 2025 ) , ADeLe places task demands and model abilities on interpretable scales to predict instance-level performance ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) , and PACE shows that a small set of non-agentic items can predict aggregate agentic benchmark scores ( Song et al., 2026 ) . These approaches map capabilities to aggregate outcomes. Process-level evaluation examines execution directly: T-Eval scores tool-use components step by step against reference trajectories ( Chen et al., 2024 ) , and AgentDiagnose scores competencies such as task decomposition, observation reading, and self-verification from agent trajectories ( Ou et al., 2025 ) . Our design additionally pairs process scores with independently measured foundational profiles for the same models. Related work also documents capability–action gaps in specific settings: strong diagnostic reasoning can coexist with weak evidence collection ( Long and Wei, 2026 ) , recognizing the need for a tool can still end in a missed call ( Cheng et al., 2026 ) , and perturbations of intermediate reasoning reveal how much later outputs depend on it ( Lanham et al., 2023 ) . We connect these lines by measuring foundational profiles, trajectory-level operations, and task outcomes under shared task conditions, then testing both capability-to-operation prediction and the incremental outcome information in operation profiles. Table 1 summarizes these differences.

blocks.en: 3.1 Foundational Capability Profile
blocks.zh: 3.1 基本能力简介

blocks.en:
Following existing capability taxonomies ( Yin et al., 2025 ; Mo et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2026 ) , we define
seven dimensions. Task Understanding (TU) recovers the objective, success
conditions, and relevant constraints. Information Selection (IS)
identifies evidence relevant to the current decision while excluding
distractors. Knowledge Use (KU) retrieves applicable parametric knowledge
or applies reliable knowledge supplied in context. Context Integration
(CI) combines the selected evidence, knowledge, prior context, and
intermediate results into a consistent representation. Reasoning (RE)
derives conclusions from that representation. Constrained Expression
(CE) realizes the conclusion while satisfying content, format, and schema
requirements. Self-Monitoring (SM) detects uncertainty, contradictions,
insufficient evidence, and candidate errors.

blocks.en: 3.2 Agentic Operation Profile
blocks.zh: 3.2 代理操作简介

blocks.en:
Agentic operations describe what the model does with these resources in a
particular trajectory. Goal Interpretation (GI) grounds subsequent
decisions in the user’s objective and constraints. State Tracking (ST)
updates the task state after new information or environment feedback.
Planning (PL) orders the steps required to reach the goal. Action
Selection (AS) chooses the next tool call or user-facing action and its
arguments. Progress Monitoring (PM) identifies what is complete, pending,
failed, or blocked. Recovery (RC) repairs a failed action or an erroneous
decision. Termination (TM) decides whether to continue, stop, or transfer.
The seven operations form a recurring control loop. State Tracking and
Progress Monitoring recur after informative transitions, while Recovery
returns control to Planning or Action Selection. Their relation to
foundational capabilities is many-to-many: one capability can support
several operations, and one operation can draw on several capabilities.

blocks.en:
Matched checkpoints hold the prior dialogue, database, available tools, and
user goal constant. Recurring differences therefore emerge during the new
continuation. Persistence across natural and checking prompts further shows
that a generic request to inspect constraints leaves the execution pattern
largely intact. The later-step reversals reveal another source of variation:
an initially compliant action can be followed by a conflicting decision.
Repeated continuations expose step-level compliance changes hidden by one
endpoint reward.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We introduce a framework linking foundational capabilities, agentic
operations, and task outcomes through capability realization gaps. In
Banking, foundational profiles explain part of operation performance, with
persistent model-level gaps across task subsets. Operation profiles add
task-score information, and shared-initial-state experiments reveal
repeatable execution differences. Local repairs produce narrower,
case-dependent effects. Agent evaluation should measure capabilities and
their reliable deployment during interaction.

blocks.en: A.2 Trajectory Annotation Protocol

blocks.en: Task contracts specify the user goal, relevant entities, constraints, required actions, and valid terminal states. Annotations use the complete chronological trajectory, with model identity and task reward hidden from the annotation input. User and tool messages supply evidence; labels evaluate the agent’s decisions and actions. A record can span several steps. The scoring evidence and label rule for each operation are given in Section 3.2 and Table 2 . Missing required actions receive zero; simulator deviations are recorded separately. The annotation pipeline automatically accepted 1,439 trajectories; twelve additional trajectories were adjudicated by an AI assistant. The AI-assisted adjudications fall outside independent human double annotation.

The checkpoint-level summary appears in
Table 15 . At the stolen-card checkpoint,
Gemini 3.1 Pro permanently blocks the card without the required
verification in all three repetitions under both natural continuation
and the checking prompt. GLM-5.2 and Claude Fable 5 avoid this violation
and leave the protective action incomplete in the first step. At the
temporary ATM-limit checkpoint, Gemini first increases the eligible
account’s limit and then also increases an ineligible account’s limit;
this recurs in both the initial short continuations and the added
repetitions. GLM and Fable avoid the corresponding invalid increase.
The latter case shows how a later action can undermine a
correct first step.
